title: A named rail infrastructure outage exposes service disruption and planned alternatives before passenger burden is measured
source_unit: Amtrak Pause for Progress A-Interlocking and First Street Tunnel infrastructure upgrade
geography: Washington, D.C.; Virginia routes and the Northeast Corridor south of Washington Union Station

denominator.unit: named A-Interlocking / First Street Tunnel operating disruption

facility.value: A-Interlocking, a critical track and control point in the First Street Tunnel south of Washington Union Station

work_scope.value: replacement of aging track switches and crossovers, tunnel track-base rehabilitation, and modern electric switch systems

scheduled_duration.unit: days; service outage from after October 16 service through before October 26 service resumes

service_disruption.value: reduced service, train cancellations, route modifications, and travel disruption south of Washington, D.C.

bus_bridge_roundtrips.unit: round-trip buses timed between Alexandria and Washington

additional_alternatives.value: two Amtrak Virginia train round trips to Alexandria, express buses from Virginia cities, a Carolinian Washington–Alexandria bus connection, Metro guidance, and rebooking/alternative-travel support

intended_reliability_benefit.value: safer, more reliable rail service and fewer delays over time

passenger_and_post_restoration_outcome.unit: missing passenger counts, delay and fare exposure, missed connections, accessibility, alternative use and adequacy, compensation, post-restoration reliability, recurrence, and acceptance

mechanism.value: A planned facility outage converts infrastructure maintenance into a dated service burden, while operator-provided bus and route alternatives create a testable mitigation stage; neither stage establishes adequate burden absorption or realized reliability benefit.

observations.method: Structured extraction from two official Amtrak pages. Facility, work scope, outage period, service disruption, alternative modes, stated future benefit, and unmeasured passenger outcomes are coded as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The sources do not provide passenger-level exposure, ridership or bus-bridge use, delay minutes, fares or extra travel cost, missed connections, accessibility, worker effects, compensation, completed work verification, post-restoration reliability, recurrence, or acceptance.
observations.subgroup: Passengers and workers using Amtrak and VRE routes between Washington and Virginia and affected Northeast Corridor/Southeast services; no affected-person denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A short coordinated outage may reduce longer-term failure risk and preserve some trips through alternatives, while the same alternatives can impose time, cost, accessibility, and capacity burdens that the public pages do not measure.

boundary: This record establishes a named Amtrak facility, a dated temporary outage, affected service, and planned alternatives. It does not establish passenger burden, mitigation adequacy, compensation, completed work, post-restoration reliability, recurrence, or public acceptance.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project follow-up memo derived from the two official Amtrak pages; passenger-level telemetry, fare records, accessibility records, and post-restoration operating data are not retained.
